verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will not land on the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'The 10-day test flight, which will not land on the moon'; R3: 'around the moon but not land there'; R4: 'won't land on the moon'; R5: 'The Artemis II crew will not land on the moon'; R6: 'crewed flyby of the Moon'; R7: 'will not land astronauts on the Moon'; R8: 'will not land on the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state no landing on the Moon, directly supporting the claim.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule will splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1 title: 'Artemis II mission to splash down off San Diego coast'; R2: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean'; R3: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean... off San Diego'; R6: 'Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego (32°18′N 117°48′W)'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm splashdown location in Pacific off San Diego.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule will splash down at the end of the Artemis II mission's 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '10-day lunar flyby... splashdown in the Pacific Ocean in 10 days’ time'; R3: '10-day mission... splashdown... on April 10'; R5: 'the mission will last approximately 10 days... by the 10th day'; R6: 'duration 9 days, 1 hour... Landing date April 11'; R7: 'last about 10 days... return to Earth for splashdown'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe a ~10-day mission ending in splashdown; R6 precise duration slightly under 10 days but commonly referred to as 10-day.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '10-day lunar flyby'; R5: 'lunar flyby'; R6: 'Crewed lunar flyby'; R7: 'free-return lunar flyby'; R8: 'lunar flyby, looping around the moon’s far side'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly describe it as a lunar flyby.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will orbit the Moon before returning to Earth.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R3: 'swing around, passing over the far side... not entering low lunar orbit'; R5: 'fly at altitudes... circle it' (flyby, not orbit); R6: 'did not enter lunar orbit'; R7: 'swing around the far side in a large figure-eight trajectory' (flyby)
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify flyby without entering lunar orbit, directly contradicting orbit claim.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission goal is a 10-day lunar flyby to test life support systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '10-day test flight... evaluate... essential life support'; R6: 'test flight... validate the Orion spacecraft's systems, crew operations'; R7: 'test the Orion spacecraft’s life support systems... 10 days... free-return lunar flyby'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm 10-day flyby mission focused on testing systems including life support.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is not a landing.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'will not land on the moon'; R3: 'not land there'; R4: 'won't land on the moon'; R5: 'will not land on the moon'; R6: 'flyby... not a landing'; R7: 'will not land astronauts on the Moon'; R8: 'will not land on the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported by explicit statements across sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II landing location is the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean'; R3: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean'; R6: 'Landing site Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego'; R7: 'parachuting into the Pacific Ocean'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm splashdown (water landing) in Pacific Ocean.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II target date is around April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R3: 'splashdown... on April 10'; R6: 'Landing date April 11, 2026, 00:07:27 UTC (April 10, 5:07:27 p.m. PDT)'
verifications.reasoning: Refers to splashdown date around April 10 (local time); launch is April 1, but context of 'land' suggests splashdown; not explicitly 'target date' but matches.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight to the Moon since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'first crewed mission to the moon in more than half a century... since Apollo 17 in December 1972'; R4: 'first humans to launch toward the moon since the Apollo 17 mission in 1972'; R5: '53 years after Apollo 17'; R6: 'first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972'; R7: 'first crewed journey beyond low Earth orbit since... 1972'; R8: 'first crewed lunar mission since 1972'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 in 1972.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will loop around the far side of the Moon.

verifications.evidence: R3: 'passing over the far side... behind the moon'; R6: 'looping around the far side... closest approach... far-side lunar surface'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe trajectory looping around far side of Moon.
